parsed.summary: This paper presents a note-grounded approach to normalize treatment-context medication mentions from clinic notes and compare them with structured EHR medication history. Using an LLM-bootstrapped, human-audited reference set, the authors show that deterministic normalization improves exact canonical agreement to 0.8429 on a held-out test set. They find that most note-to-structured-record mismatches are explained by semantic relatedness or temporal displacement rather than complete documentation failure.

chk_problem.value: Disagreement between clinic notes and structured EHR medication history due to normalization errors, terminology differences, or timing.
chk_problem.paper_quote: Same-visit disagreement between these sources may result from note-side normalization errors, differences in terminology or timing, or actual differences in documentation.

chk_method.value: A note-grounded approach combining LLM-assisted reference construction, human review, deterministic normalization, and semantic-temporal comparisons.
chk_method.paper_quote: We developed a note-grounded approach that uses large language model (LLM)-assisted reference construction, targeted and random human review, deterministic medication normalization, and semantic and temporal comparisons with structured medication history.

chk_data.value: A frozen cohort of 11,812 eligible visits from 761 patients and 22,483 clinic notes.
chk_data.paper_quote: We conducted a clinic-note-only evaluation of treatment-context medication normalization using a frozen cohort run of 11,812 eligible visits from 761 patients and 22,483 manifest notes.

chk_setup.value: Evaluation of the deterministic canonicalization pipeline on a held-out test split of 5,403 reference mention rows.
chk_setup.paper_quote: We evaluated the deterministic canonicalization pipeline and its calibration comparators on the held-out test split of 5,403 reference mention rows with non-empty project-specific canonical medication labels.

chk_primary_result.value: Exact canonical agreement improved from 0.7226 with surface-exact matching to 0.8429 after lexical cleanup and curated alias mapping.
chk_primary_result.paper_quote: On 5,403 held-out mention rows, exact canonical agreement improved from 0.7226 with surface-exact matching to 0.8429 after lexical cleanup and curated alias mapping.

chk_secondary_result.value: Only 16.44% of note-derived rows had same-visit exact overlap with structured history, but 55.17% had same-visit semantic overlap and 90.34% had same-visit or ±30-day overlap.
chk_secondary_result.paper_quote: In the full-cohort characterization analysis, only 16.44% of note-derived rows had same-visit exact overlap with structured medication history, but 55.17% had same-visit semantic overlap, 90.34% had same-visit or ±30-day overlap, and only 3.97% remained in the strict no-structured-overlap bucket under broad project-level mapping.

chk_baseline.value: Public OMOP/RxNorm synonym matching and generic nearest-canonical lexical retrieval based on character n-grams, edit similarity, and token overlap.
chk_baseline.paper_quote: To calibrate the deterministic gain, we also evaluated public OMOP/RxNorm synonym matching without project-specific alias refinement and generic nearest-canonical lexical retrieval based on character n-grams, edit similarity, and token overlap.

chk_conclusion.value: Evidence characterization should precede downstream clinical inference when comparing clinic-note medication evidence with structured medication history.
chk_conclusion.paper_quote: These results suggest that evidence characterization should precede downstream clinical inference when clinic-note medication evidence is compared with structured medication history.

chk_limitation.value: The cohort is from a private single-center clinic-note environment, and the canonical label space and categories are project-specific.
chk_limitation.paper_quote: The cohort comes from a private single-center clinic-note environment, and both the canonical label space and broad medication categories are project-specific.
